source.title: Experience Makes Skillful: Enabling Generalizable Medical Agent Reasoning via Self-Evolving Skill Memory

observations.text: SkeMex makes memory use explicitly context-conditioned before action: at episode onset it extracts a clinical category, restricts task-level retrieval to the corresponding branch, removes skills outside the current context, and applies category-conditioned utility to general skills because broad principles can vary in effectiveness across clinical domains. Informative failures are retained, while admitted skill drafts must state a situational trigger and concrete clinical steps.

Table 11 provides matched retrieval-component evidence: full SkeMex averages 53.22, Similarity Only 47.64 (-5.58), Utility Only 48.30 (-4.92), LLM Ranking Only 50.93, and w/o Prescreen 50.69. The paper interprets similarity-only retrieval as vulnerable to topically close but ineffective skills and utility-only retrieval as vulnerable to historically successful but context-mismatched overly general procedures.

Memory admission/governance also matters in reported ablations: full SkeMex averages 53.22 versus 48.82 without Draft Review, 47.56 without Buffer Gating, and 49.27 without Deprecation. These interventions affect memory quality/lifecycle, not solely receiver-side revalidation of a fixed retrieved record.

The strongest SkeMex evidence is still retrieval-side/context-routing evidence rather than the target frontier: it does not hold the same stored and retrieved failure record fixed while changing only a receiver-side accept/reject applicability predicate. Therefore it strengthens the target-applicability invariant but does not close the science-domain matched-revalidation gap.

protocol_inferences.name: CONTEXT_CONDITIONED_MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_IS_NOT_POST_RETRIEVAL_AUTHORIZATION
protocol_inferences.text: Context-aware routing and utility conditioning can reduce mismatched memory use, but their evidence must not be generalized into a claim that a post-retrieval receiver-side applicability/authorization gate has been causally validated.

protocol_inferences.name: FAILURE_MEMORY_TRIGGER_FIELD
protocol_inferences.text: Failure-derived operational memory should retain an explicit situational trigger/applicability statement in addition to provenance; relevance scoring alone should not erase the condition under which the record was learned.

phase1_acceptance.reason: SkeMex is evidence about memory architecture, not a zero-dependency scheduled-Chat replay mechanism; the demonstrated system relies on model/tool execution and does not isolate the exact receiver-side accept/reject intervention sought by this role.
phase1_acceptance.useful_evidence: Context-conditioned retrieval and memory-quality governance provide science-domain quantitative support for keeping applicability metadata operational rather than decorative.

scope_notes: Do not interpret the ablations as holding the retrieved record fixed; candidate selection/scoring or repository governance changes.
Do not infer that SkeMex itself satisfies zero-monthly-quota or zero-external-executor Phase-1 acceptance.
The public-code status was not used as substantive evidence because no exact official implementation revision was established in the checked search.
